replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
There is only so much LLMs can do with code in order to create models and animations. The more complex you get, the more the tokens go up and the more likely things just fall apart. Right now it might take you 120k tokens to have the AI sculpt out a wolf in blender, and that might be a $5 request. Meanwhile you can get a higher quality mesh sculpt out of Tripo for 30 cents alongside textures (though I admit I find the textures in need of serious touch up).

The technology is just fundamentally different and while a blender or Three.JS approach with materials and python or js coded elements is a viable pipeline for llms. It does not produce realistic graphics, and if it did it would take an astronomical number of tokens.

Don't take that as me talking down on the model though. From everything I've seen it looks to be very impressive. But as an example I saw it did an outstanding job on the BuseyBench. But it took a cool 36k tokens (almost 2 dollars), and 10.5 minutes. And the quality was less than original Stable Diffusion which could be run for like .0001 cents right now on a local machine to do the same thing in half a second. This could still be valuable if, say, the SVG was well separated into sensible parts. But I'm not so sure it was. It's really the only model that's created a reasonable interpretation, however.

comments.author: AesonMeric
comments.body: How the hell did this thing make the animations? Is it ik or fk? Did it check it's results and polished? Did it just pilot the rig like a damn robot? I'm a 3d animator and this is wild to me.

replies.author: Snoo-29395
replies.body:
This is the AI response:

It’s a hybrid setup. The hands and elbows use IK, while the weapon and moving parts use direct control/FK animation. I scripted the repetitive mechanical motion, evaluated the rig frame by frame, then baked the gun and arms into paired animation clips.

It definitely wasn’t just blindly piloting every bone. I directed the key poses, timing, anticipation, impact, recoil, and recovery, then rendered and reviewed the results. I also checked hand contact and FBX round-tripping. The melee animation actually went through a couple of revisions after visual review exposed problems.

replies.author: Snoo-29395
replies.body:
Honestly? No clue, because it did everything behind the curtains.

Now playing a lot with it, it's really good at generating concept arts through images, so my new workflow is:

\- Take a screenshot of my game  
\- Ask for what i want, but start asking to make a concept art with it.  
\- Once the concept art looks good enough, ask to make an actual texture and model diagram concept from it  
\- move to blender, ask to replicate the concept using the mcp  
\- add animations or everything i want  
\- done, ready to export

I really simplified the process, but i'm learning while making, so probably other folks with come with better workflows in the coming days
